search_strategy: Systematic full-corpus dump-then-grep, in the right order for this world's traps. Cloned the repo and read the target files/history/issues first (Gitea search API returned nothing useful, so it dumped all 736 issues+comments locally and grepped). Dumped BookStack wiki pages, discovered on the first pass that its dump script had lost the comments field (BookStack's active/archived comment structure), and explicitly re-fetched /api/pages/{id} for every page to recover comments -- this is exactly the trap the world sets ('BookStack search does not index comments') and the agent caught it before it cost anything, recovering both wiki-comment remarks (g3.r1.l5, g3.r2.s1a). Dumped IMAP mail (119 messages) and grepped for retry/throttle/jitter keywords, finding both mail threads (revoked-key/l8, smoke-run-timings/l12, 429-handling/s4d). Dumped Mattermost chat across all 12 channels via the admin/system-endpoint route (after discovering the admin wasn't a channel member), normalized escaped newlines, mapped user ids to names, then ran a long sequence of increasingly targeted greps (retry_policy|waiver|throttle|classif|verdict|failure_class|cooldown; retry.after|retry_after; time_of_last_rate_limit_error|cool_down|pause; attempts_made|pass count; attempts_left; reset) and read the surrounding exchange for every hit, eventually consolidating everything into /tmp/retry_chat.txt and reading it end to end. This combination of exhaustive grep + full-context reads + a dedicated wiki-comments recovery pass is why all 49 remarks and all 4 herring/reversal pairs surfaced.
